findings.reason: without the bound on the arm where the 381 GB was measured, the node can pass on its headline number while leaving the memory barrier it was dispatched to remove.
findings.text: §3 done-when (1) bounds the H200 arm by wall and executable only ("at most 60 s on the H200") while §0 (line 47) declares the plan owns "at most 64 GB resident on the host during a cold compile"; the 381 GB figure this plan exists to remove is host memory and the batch program is the program that produced it, so a build that compiles in 55 s and holds 300 GB would pass

findings.reason: a worker sizes a "64-node" job as a small one and loses it, or reports the base arm unmeasured, leaving done-when (2) unsatisfiable.
findings.text: §3 done-when (2)'s base arm is "the base program evaluated over those nodes alone in one bounded job", but §3's own line 62 states the cost is node-count-independent, so a 64-node base build pays the same 7,044 s cold compile and ~381 GB as the 2,132-node one; the clause states no job size and the only recorded job of that shape (sirius 1290676, 450 GB, 5 h) is the one that failed to publish its rows

findings.reason: the conclusion (expanded-equation count does not set compile time) still follows from the inlining result, and §5 states the experiment correctly, so only §3's one-line paraphrase is wrong.
findings.text: §3 cites §5 as showing that "removing the top-ranked term's tangent left the compile unchanged", but the measured experiment inlined `_harmonic_pair_step` (comment c-run-r-20261026T214731173490, line 111: "Inlining the serial harmonic pair step ... trims H200 cold compile from 82.43 s to 82.36 s"), and no tangent removal was run
